items.title: Enable paging for the managed-network outbound-rule batch action
items.summary: Adds @list to the existing asynchronous batchOutboundRules action on a Cognitive Services account's managed network. The action still updates outbound rules with the same request and response wire shapes, but now advertises paging over OutboundRuleListResult.value and nextLink. Generated SDK consumption changes from an LRO returning the response envelope to an LRO with paged outbound-rule items. Both sides compile API version 2026-03-01; this is not a new resource-list lifecycle operation or an API-version addition.

guidance.excerpt: To enable pagination for an operation the first step is to decorate it with the @list decorator and have the return type contain a property decorated with @pageItems

For HTTP services, @nextLink (and other link decorators like @prevLink, @firstLink, @lastLink) should be followed using a GET request by default. The link URIs are expected to be treated as opaque URLs that contain all necessary information to navigate to the respective page.

intentAssessments.expected: Use @list on the operation to enable pagination with recognized page items; follow HTTP next links using GET by default. Preserve the resource action's identity and distinguish existing-version wire compatibility from generated SDK effects.
intentAssessments.actual: The added @list precedes post is ArmResourceActionAsync with @action("batchOutboundRules"). Canonical compiler facts recognize OutboundRuleListResult.value as page items, nextLink as continuation, and GET as its continuation verb. The existing 2026-03-01 wire contract is unchanged apart from paging metadata.
intentAssessments.rationale: The change matches the fetched low-level pagination and decorator guidance while retaining its resource-scoped action role. Although the query labels the service data-plane, the declaration is ARM; no data-plane operation-template requirement is transferred to it. Evolving APIs was reviewed first for existing-version implications, but its guidance does not establish that adding paging metadata to an unchanged wire contract requires a new API version. The independently confirmed generated SDK breaks are not treated as automatic Azure Guidelines violations. This conclusion concerns the supplied specification evidence, not unobserved service implementation behavior.
